sources.title: AFI Catalog: It's a Wonderful Life (1946)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, source history, production context and practical-effects note.
supports: James Stewart is credited as George Bailey.
Philip Van Doren Stern's story The Greatest Gift is the source material, and Stewart's role followed four years of World War II service.
Liberty Films was the first production of a company begun by Capra, Wyler, Stevens and Briskin; AFI records artificial snow made with limestone and white plaster.
limits: George Bailey, Clarence and Bedford Falls are fictional narrative elements.
Stewart's military service is performer/production context, not biographical evidence about George.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: It's a Wonderful Life (1946)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected role, official synopsis, literary basis and nominations.
supports: The Academy identifies George Bailey as James Stewart and Clarence as the guardian angel who intervenes.
It identifies Philip Van Doren Stern's The Greatest Gift as the basis for the film.
It records five nominations, including Actor for Stewart, Directing for Capra and Best Picture.
limits: The page is an event overview; it does not establish a real-world factual account behind the fantasy narrative.
The listed awards are nominations, not wins for Stewart or the film.

source_link.title: Academy: «Эта замечательная жизнь» (1946)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Стюарта как Джорджа, роль Кларенса, источник Стерна и пять номинаций.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Deer Hunter (1978)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, awards/reception history and credited post-production information.
supports: Robert De Niro is credited as Michael Vronsky.
AFI records De Niro's Actor nomination and awards for Best Picture, Directing, Supporting Actor and Sound.
AFI documents divided critical reaction and protests connected to the film's depiction of Vietnamese people.
limits: Michael Vronsky and the plot are fictional, and reception controversy does not establish the historical accuracy of the film's Vietnam-war representation.
AFI's reception history should be attributed to recorded contemporaneous responses.

source_link.supports: Подтверждает Роберта Де Ниро — Майкла Вронски, наградный контекст и документированную реакцию на фильм.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: The 51st Academy Awards (1979)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected release-year statement, leading-actor category and film award ledger.
supports: The ceremony honors films released in 1978.
Robert De Niro was nominated for Actor in a Leading Role and Christopher Walken won supporting actor for The Deer Hunter.
The film had nine nominations and five wins, including Best Picture, Directing, Film Editing and Sound.
limits: De Niro's listing is a nomination, not a win.
The award ledger is not evidence for plot detail or historical accuracy.
